question: What is the area of the segment formed by a chord in a circle of radius 12 cm, if the angle subtended at the center is 150°?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the Area of a Segment:

⇒ Area = r² × [(π × θ ÷ 360°) − (sin θ ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 12² × [(π × 150° ÷ 360°) − (sin 150° ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 144 × [(5π ÷ 12) − (1 ÷ 4)]

⇒ Area = 60π − 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60π−36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Area of Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

**Given:**

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = 12 cm

⇒ Angle subtended at the center (θ) = 150°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of Sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × r² × sin θ

⇒ Area of Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of Sector = (150° ÷ 360°) × π × 12²

⇒ Area of Sector = (5 ÷ 12) × π × 144 = 60π cm²

⇒ To find the area of the triangle, we use sin(150°) = sin(180° − 30°) = sin(30°) = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 12² × (1 ÷ 2)

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 144 × (1 ÷ 2) = 36 cm²

⇒ Area of Segment = 60π − 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60π−36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Major Segment

It is calculated by subtracting the area of the minor segment from the total area of the circle: Area = πr² − Area of Minor Segment.

Length of an Arc

The arc length corresponding to a central angle θ is a fraction of the circle's circumference: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The boundary length of a sector comprises the arc length and two radii: Perimeter = L + 2r.
